info.name: Places API
info.description:
Complete Postman collection for the **Places** mobile REST API (`routes/api.php`).

## How auth works in this API
1. **`x-secret-key`** header — required by the `appSecret` middleware on almost every route (must equal the server's `API_SECRET_KEY` env var). This collection injects it automatically via each protected folder's pre-request script, sourced from the `api_secret_key` collection variable — set that variable once and every request in the folder picks it up.
2. **`x-language`** header (`ar`/`en`) — read by `ApiLocaleKeyMiddleware` on *every* `/api/*` route (in or out of the appSecret group) to set the response locale. Auto-injected collection-wide from the `language` variable.
3. **Bearer token** (Laravel Sanctum) — required by the *Customer* and *Booking* folders. Obtained by running **Auth > Request OTP -> Verify OTP -> (Register Customer if new)**; the token is auto-captured into the `customer_token` variable by each request's test script. It's applied explicitly on every request in those two folders (not just inherited from the folder) so it can never silently go missing.
4. **`Accept: application/json`** — injected collection-wide. Important: `bootstrap/app.php` calls `redirectGuestsTo(fn () => route('home'))`, so an unauthenticated request that *doesn't* send `Accept: application/json` gets a `302` redirect to the website homepage instead of a clean `401` JSON — Postman would silently follow it and show you a confusing `200 OK` full of HTML. This header prevents that.

## Response envelope
Most endpoints return `{ "success": bool, "message": string, "data": any, "errors"?: any }` (see `App\Traits\ApiResponse`). Exceptions are noted per-endpoint: Guesty proxy endpoints and the Geidea/OwnerRez webhooks return raw/simple JSON instead, and `POST /customer/register` falls back to Laravel's default `{message, errors}` shape on validation failure.

## Suggested end-to-end flow to test
1. **Auth** folder: Request OTP -> Verify OTP (use the `2020` bypass code to skip real SMS) -> Register Customer if it's a new phone number.
2. **Home** folder: Home Index / Get Apartment Details to pick a real `apartment_id`.
3. **Booking** folder: Determine Booking Status -> Calculate Price -> Add Booking -> (complete payment out-of-band or send a synthetic **Geidea Payment Webhook**) -> Cancel Booking.
4. **Customer** folder: Get All Bookings / Current Bookings to confirm state.

## Known issues documented inline
- `POST /booking/booking-services` is a **dead route** (controller method doesn't exist) — see its description.
- `POST /customer/notification/mark-seen/{id}` and `GET /customer/notification/unread-count` have an argument-order bug that can turn a clean 404/422 into a 500 — see their descriptions.
- `GET /test` and `GET /test2` are completely unauthenticated debug endpoints.

item.name: 1. Auth (OTP + Registration)
item.description: Public within the appSecret group — no bearer token needed yet.

request.description:
Sends a 4-digit OTP via SMS to the given phone number.

**Validation:** `phone` required, must pass the `phone` rule (propaganistas/laravel-phone). Arabic-Indic digits are auto-converted to Western digits before validation.

**Status codes:**
- `200` OTP sent. `data.has_account` tells the client whether to route to login or registration after verify.
- `400` Validation failed (invalid/missing phone) OR OTP provider failed to send — body: `{success:false, errors:[], message:"..."}`.
- `500` Unexpected exception while sending (e.g. SMS gateway down).

**Tip:** every response also carries `x-app-version` / `x-update-required` headers (from `APP_VERSION` / `UPDATE_REQUIRED` env vars).

request.description:
Verifies the OTP for a phone number.

**Validation:** `phone` required+phone rule, `otp` required digits:4, `fcm_token` nullable.

**Master bypass code:** submitting `otp = 2020` always succeeds regardless of the real OTP — a QA/testing shortcut baked into `AuthController::verifyOtp()`. Use it to skip real SMS delivery in this collection.

**Branches:**
- Existing customer -> `200` with `data.customer`, `data.token` (Sanctum bearer token), `data.register_required=false`. The request's test script auto-saves `customer_token`.
- New phone -> `200` with `data.token` (a short-lived **registration** token cached 10 minutes), `data.register_required=true`. The test script auto-saves it to `verify_token` for the next **Register Customer** call.

**Status codes:**
- `200` verified (see branches above).
- `422` wrong/expired OTP or validation exception — body: `{success:false, errors:{...}, message:"..."}`.
- `500` unexpected exception.

request.description:
Completes registration for a phone number that was just OTP-verified (`register_required=true`).

**Validation:** `token` required (the `verify_token` from step 2 — looked up via `Cache::pull('verified_api_phone_'.token)`, single-use, ~10 min TTL), `first_name`/`last_name` required, letters (Arabic or Latin) + spaces only via regex, `email` required unique, `fcm_token` nullable.

**Important:** unlike the other Auth endpoints, this action does **not** wrap `$request->validate()` in a try/catch, so validation failures return Laravel's **default** Form Request 422 envelope (`{message, errors}`), not the app's usual `{success, errors, message, data}` shape.

**Status codes:**
- `200` created — `data.customer`, `data.token` (Sanctum bearer token). Test script auto-saves `customer_token`.
- `422` Laravel default validation error shape (see note above), OR custom `{success:false}` 422 if the token is missing/expired (`auth.phone_required_or_expired`).
- `500` unexpected exception (e.g. race on unique email).

request.description:
Marks a notification as seen for the authenticated customer.

**Status codes:**
- `200` marked as seen.
- `404` notification not found.
- `422` already marked as seen.
- `401` unauthenticated.

**Known bug:** the not-found and already-seen branches call `errorResponse('message', code, [])` — arguments in the **wrong order** for the trait's `errorResponse($errors, $message, $status)` signature. Passing an array where an int `$status` is expected throws a `TypeError`, so in practice these two branches are likely to surface as a generic **`500`** instead of a clean `404`/`422`. Treat an unexpected 500 here as "not found" or "already seen" until fixed server-side.

request.description:
Creates a **pending** booking + payment transaction, then returns the payment gateway's hosted checkout URL.

**Validation:** `apartment_id` required exists, `check_in`/`check_out` required dates, `adults_count` required int >=1, `children_count` required int >=0, `coupon_code` nullable exists:coupons,code, `notes` nullable, `booking_source` nullable in `web,android,ios`, `payment_method_code` required (currently only `geidea` is configured in `config/payments.php`).

- `200` payment URL created. Test script saves `booking_id`.
- `400`/generic `errorResponse` on: overlapping dates, invalid coupon, OwnerRez unavailable, payment gateway failure — message varies (`api.already_booked`, `api.apartment_not_available_external`, `api.payment_creation_failed`, etc).
- `401` unauthenticated. `422` validation.

request.description:
Customer-initiated cancellation of an **approved & paid** booking. Sets `status = customer_canceled`, `refund_status = pending`, `refund_amount = final_price`, and emails the building supervisor (best-effort; email failure does not fail the request).

**Validation:** `booking_id` required exists:bookings,id.

**Eligibility (`Booking::canBeCanceled()`):**
- `status` must be `approved` AND `payment_status` must be `paid`.
- No **open** date-change request on the booking (must be resolved first).
- Must be cancelled at least `cancel_before_hours` (settings table, default 24) before check-in time (booking's own check-in time, default `16:00` if unset).

**Status codes:**
- `200` cancelled — returns the refreshed `BookingResource` with `refund_status`/`refund_amount`/`can_cancel=false`.
- `400` booking not found/not owned (`api.booking_not_found`) OR not cancellable per the rules above (`api.booking_cannot_be_canceled`).
- `401` unauthenticated. `422` validation.

This is the primary endpoint for the current `booking-cancellation-and-geidea-refund` feature branch — refund settlement itself happens out-of-band via the admin/Geidea refund flow, not in this call.

item.description: Outside the appSecret group — no x-secret-key needed. These are normally hit by a browser/webview redirect from the payment gateway, not called directly by app code.

request.description:
Browser-redirect endpoint the payment gateway sends the customer back to after checkout. Not typically called directly from Postman — included for completeness/manual testing.

**Behavior:** if the Geidea webhook already confirmed the booking, redirects straight to **Payment Success**. Otherwise it does a manual `handleCallBack()` check with the gateway; on success it completes the booking and redirects to success, else redirects to **Payment Failed**.

**Status codes:** `302` redirect to success or failed route. `404`/error if `{{payment_method_code}}` isn't a configured gateway (`config('payments.gateways')` — currently only `geidea`).

Postman follows redirects by default; check the final response or disable redirect-following to inspect the `Location` header.

item.name: 8. Webhooks & OAuth (server-to-server)
item.description: Outside the appSecret group entirely — these use their own auth (Basic Auth for OwnerRez, live API re-verification for Geidea).

request.description:
Server-to-server webhook Geidea calls after a payment attempt. **Not protected by `x-secret-key`** — instead the handler re-verifies the payment status directly against the Geidea API (`GeideaPayment::verifyPayment()`) before trusting the payload, so a spoofed POST alone can't fake a paid booking.

**Behavior:**
- Looks up the `Transaction` by `orderId` (or falls back to `merchantReferenceId`), locked `FOR UPDATE` inside a DB transaction to avoid double-processing concurrent webhook deliveries.
- If the transaction is tied to a **date-change surcharge** request, applies the new dates via `DateChangeService::confirmSurchargePayment()` instead of the normal booking-confirmation path.
- Otherwise completes the booking (`BookingService::completeBookingAfterPayment()`) and emails the customer + building supervisor.

**Status codes:** always `200`, with a `status` field indicating outcome — `ignored` (no orderId / transaction not found), `not_paid` (Geidea says it isn't Paid yet), `already_processed`, or `ok`. This endpoint intentionally never surfaces errors as non-200 (webhook senders typically retry on non-2xx).

**Testing note:** since the handler re-verifies against the live Geidea API, POSTing a synthetic payload here from Postman will resolve to `not_paid`/`ignored` unless there's a real matching Geidea order — use this mainly to inspect the response contract, not to actually confirm a booking.
